title: Converbs II and helper verbs
seoTitle: Turkmen helper verbs: okap gör, ýazyp ber
intro: This unit adds two more ways to join clauses, **because** with `-dYgY üçin` (*Wagty ýokdugy üçin gelmedi*, he didn't come because he had no time) and **as soon as** with `-An badyna` (*Öýe gelen badyna uklady*, she fell asleep as soon as she got home). Then come converbs said twice for actions done over and over (*dura-dura*, *gaýtalap-gaýtalap*), and five helper verbs that follow `-(Y)p` and give the main verb a shade of meaning: *okap gör* (try reading it), *ýazyp ber* (write it down for me), *ýazyp al* (write it down, for yourself), *alyp goý* (buy in advance), *gülüp goýber* (burst out laughing).

blocks.text: You know two ways to give a reason ([A1 unit 12](a1-u12)): *sebäbi* (because) and *şonuň üçin* (so, that's why). A third packs the reason into one clause before the main verb. It is the `-dYgY` of [B1 unit 6](b1-u06), with its possessive ending, then *üçin* (for): *Wagty ýokdugy üçin gelmedi*, he didn't come because he had no time.

Everything works as in [B1 unit 6](b1-u06): `-An` for the past, `-ýAn` for the present, `-jAk` for the future, and `-dYgY` straight after a noun, an adjective, *ýok* or *däl*. For **not**, use `-mAýAn` (*gelmeýändigi üçin*, because he isn't coming) or *ýok* and *däl* (*pulumyň ýokdugy üçin*, because I have no money); for a past **not**, this course says it with *sebäbi*: *Biz gitmedik, sebäbi ol gelmedi*. The possessive says who: *gijä galandygym üçin*, because **I** was late; *gijä galandygy üçin*, because **he** or **she** was late. When the reason has its own doer, it goes in the genitive: *Aýnanyň kesel bolandygy üçin, biz gitmedik* (because Aýna was ill, we didn't go). When both halves share the subject, say it once, at the start: *Aýna kesel bolandygy üçin işe gelmedi*.

items.en: He didn't come because he had no time.
We stayed at home because it was raining.

items.tk: Aýna kesel bolandygy üçin işe gelmedi.
items.seg: Aýna kesel bol|an|dyg|y üçin iş|e gel|me|di.
items.en: Aýna didn't come to work because she was ill.

items.tk: Kakam lukmandygy üçin gije hem işleýär.
items.seg: Kaka|m lukman|dyg|y üçin gije hem işle|ýär.
items.en: My father works at night too, because he is a doctor.

items.tk: Biz Mara göçjekdigimiz üçin öýümizi satýarys.
items.seg: Biz Mar|a göç|jek|dig|imiz üçin öý|ümiz|i sat|ýar|ys.
items.en: We're selling our house because we're going to move to Mary.

blocks.title: Three ways to say because
blocks.text: *Gelmedi, sebäbi wagty ýokdy.* *Wagty ýokdy, şonuň üçin gelmedi.* *Wagty ýokdugy üçin gelmedi.* All three say the same thing. The last makes one sentence of the two and is common in writing. You will also meet a shorter form with `-An` and the possessive: *gijä galyp gelenim üçin*, because I came late.

blocks.title: No accusative before üçin
blocks.text: After *bilmek* the clause takes the accusative (*gelendigini bilýärin*), but *üçin* takes none: *gelendigi üçin*, not `gelendigini üçin`. And keep the possessive: *gijä galandygym üçin*, not `gijä galandyk üçin`.

*Badyna* after a verb in `-An` means **as soon as**: *Öýe gelen badyna uklady* (she fell asleep as soon as she got home), *Kino gutaran badyna, zal boşady* (as soon as the film ended, the hall emptied). *Bat* is speed, so *badyna* is literally **at its speed**: the second action follows at once.

The verb in `-An` takes no case and no ending: *gelen badyna*. Its spelling is that of *gelen* ([B1 unit 5](b1-u05)): *okan*, *işlän*, *giden*, *eşiden*. As with the other converbs, the subject goes at the start, each half can have its own, and the last verb gives the tense: *Men öýe gelen badyna, saňa jaň ederin* (I'll call you as soon as I get home).

items.en: She fell asleep as soon as she got home.
As soon as the film ended, the hall emptied.

items.tk: Bu habary eşiden badyna, kakama jaň etdim.
items.seg: Bu habar|y eşid|en badyna, kaka|m|a jaň et|di|m.
items.en: As soon as I heard the news, I called my father.
As soon as the child saw me, he laughed.

items.tk: Men öýe gelen badyna, saňa jaň ederin.
items.seg: Men öý|e gel|en badyna, saňa jaň ed|er|in.
items.en: I'll call you as soon as I get home.

blocks.title: When, after, as soon as
blocks.text: *Öýe gelende* (when I got home), *öýe gelenden soň* (after I got home), *öýe gelen badyna* (as soon as I got home, at once). The last one leaves no gap between the two actions.

blocks.title: Two words, no case
blocks.text: *Gelen badyna*, with the participle as it is: not `gelende badyna` or `gelenden badyna`. And *badyna* comes after the verb, never before it.

sections.title: Again and again: converbs said twice

blocks.text: A converb said twice means an action done over and over, or for a long time, often until it has an effect: *Dura-dura ýadadym*, I got tired from standing (and waiting) so long. Turkmen writes the pair with a hyphen.

Two converbs are doubled this way. `-A` goes on stems that end in a consonant: *dur-* → *dura-dura*, *git-* → *gide-gide* (with the soft *t*), *gül-* → *güle-güle*, *aýt-* → *aýda-aýda*. You won't meet `-A` on its own in this course; learn the pairs. `-(Y)p` can be doubled on any verb, including those that end in a vowel: *gaýtalap-gaýtalap*, repeating over and over; *okap-okap*, reading and reading.

blocks.caption: Converbs said twice
head: Pair
Meaning
rows: standing and standing, waiting a long time
going on and on; in time, in the end

items.en: I got tired from standing so long.
I learn new words by repeating them over and over.
I'm tired of telling him again and again; he doesn't listen.
The children were playing and laughing.

blocks.title: The same form twice, with a hyphen
blocks.text: Both halves have the same shape: *dura-dura*, not `dura durup`; *gaýtalap-gaýtalap*, not `gaýtalap gaýtalady`. And they don't take an ending: the last verb does.

sections.title: Helper verbs after -(Y)p: try, for someone, for yourself, ready, at once

blocks.text: You already know helpers after `-(Y)p`: *bilmek* for **can** (*ýüzüp bilýärin*, [A2 unit 5](a2-u05)) and *otyr, dur, ýatyr, ýör* for what is going on (*okap otyr*, [A2 unit 11](a2-u11)). Five more verbs, used after `-(Y)p`, lose some of their own meaning and add a shade to the main verb: *görmek*, *bermek*, *almak*, *goýmak* and *goýbermek*. The main verb stays in `-(Y)p`; the helper takes the tense and the person: *okap gördüm*, *okap gör!*, *okap görersiňmi?*

**görmek: try it and see.** After `-(Y)p`, *görmek* (to see) means **try doing it, to see what it's like**: *Okap gör!*, give it a read! In the past, above all in questions, it means **have you ever done it**: *Sen düýä münüp gördüňmi?*, have you ever ridden a camel?

blocks.caption: `-(Y)p görmek`: try it and see
head: Turkmen
English
rows: Try reading it! Give it a read!
Taste the palaw (and see what you think).
Men ony çözüp gördüm, ýöne başarmadym.
I tried solving it, but I couldn't.
Have you ever ridden a camel?

blocks.title: Try: görmek or synanyşmak?
blocks.text: English has one **try** for both. *Gelmäge synanyşdym* ([B1 unit 4](b1-u04)): I tried to come, I made an effort, maybe in vain. *Iýip gördüm*: I tried it, I tasted it to see what it was like.

**bermek: for someone.** After `-(Y)p`, *bermek* (to give) says the action is done for someone else, as a favour: *Maňa ýazyp ber*, write it down for me. English shows this with **for me**, or with the order of **bought me a phone**; sometimes it shows nothing at all.

blocks.caption: `-(Y)p bermek`: for someone
head: Turkmen
English
rows: The teacher explained the rule to us.

blocks.text: **almak: for yourself, to keep.** After `-(Y)p`, *almak* (to take) says you do it for your own use, so that you have it: *Nomerimi ýazyp al*, write down my number. Compare *ýazyp ber*, write it down **for me**, with *ýazyp al*, write it down **for yourself**. With *basmak* (to press) it gives *basyp almak*, to take by force, to capture.

blocks.caption: `-(Y)p almak`: for yourself
head: Turkmen
English
rows: I wrote down what the teacher said.
Make a note: the lesson is at nine.

blocks.text: **goýmak: ready, for later, left that way.** After `-(Y)p`, *goýmak* (to put) says the result stays in place for later: done in advance, put away, or left as it is. *Men biletleri alyp goýdum*: I've bought the tickets, they're ready.

blocks.caption: `-(Y)p goýmak`: ready, for later
head: Turkmen
English
rows: I bought the tickets in advance.
We've cooked a meal for the guests; it's ready.
Just so you know: there's no class tomorrow.

blocks.text: **goýbermek: let go, all at once.** On its own, *goýbermek* means to let go, to release: *Meni goýber!*, let me go! After `-(Y)p` it says the action goes off at once and completely, often suddenly, without holding back: *Ol gülüp goýberdi*, she burst out laughing.

blocks.caption: `-(Y)p goýbermek`: at once, without holding back
head: Turkmen
English
rows: Dad sold off his old car.

blocks.title: When English can't show it
blocks.text: Often English has no word for the helper: *Nahar bişirip goýdum* and *Nahar bişirdim* are both **I've cooked a meal**. The helper adds a shade you feel more than translate. This course accepts the plain English for both, and from English it accepts the plain verb too, unless the English asks for the shade: **for me**, **in advance**, **try**, **burst out**.

blocks.title: The helper takes the endings
blocks.text: *Okap gördüm*, not `okadym gördüm`; *ýazyp beriň*, not `ýazyň beriň`. And keep *goýmak* and *goýbermek* apart: *alyp goýdum*, I bought it (to keep); *satyp goýberdim*, I sold it off.

lines.tk: Bu palawy dadyp gör! Ejäm bişirip berdi.
lines.en: Taste this palaw! Mum made it for us.

lines.tk: Örän tagamly! Maňa onuň reseptini ýazyp berersiňmi?
lines.en: It's delicious! Will you write down the recipe for me?

lines.tk: Bolýar, ýöne ilki ejämden sorap göreýin.
lines.en: OK, but let me ask Mum first and see.

lines.tk: Sag bol! Men ony ýazyp alaryn we öýde bişirip görerin.
lines.en: Thanks! I'll write it down and try making it at home.
No, but I'm going to try to learn!

summary: **Because**: `-dYgY` with the possessive, then *üçin*: *gijä galandygym üçin*, *wagty ýokdugy üçin*; no accusative before *üçin*.
**As soon as**: `-An badyna`: *öýe gelen badyna*, *eşiden badyna*.
A converb said twice, with a hyphen, is an action repeated or drawn out: *dura-dura*, *gide-gide*, *gaýtalap-gaýtalap*.
After `-(Y)p`, the helper takes the tense and the person: *okap gördüm*, *ýazyp beriň*.
*görmek*: try it and see (*dadyp gör*); in the past, have you ever (*münüp gördüňmi?*).
*bermek*: for someone (*ýazyp ber*); *almak*: for yourself (*ýazyp al*), and *basyp almak*, to capture.
*goýmak*: ready, in advance, left that way (*alyp goýdum*, *açyp goýdy*); *goýbermek*: at once, without holding back (*gülüp goýberdi*), and on its own, to let go.
